text: कल मुझे दिल्ली जाना है।
expected_pronunciation_notes: Standard Hindi declarative.

text: क्या आप मुझे पानी दे सकते हैं?
expected_pronunciation_notes: Polite Hindi question.

text: मेरा भाई आज स्कूल नहीं गया क्योंकि उसकी तबीयत खराब है।
expected_pronunciation_notes: Long Hindi sentence with English loanword \"स्कूल\" written in Devanagari.

text: मेरे पास सिर्फ़ तीन सौ रुपये हैं, बस इतने में चला लो।
expected_pronunciation_notes: Numerals expressed in Devanagari words; casual register.

text: जल्दी आओ यार, सब तेरा इंतज़ार कर रहे हैं।
expected_pronunciation_notes: Casual imperative with informal pronoun \"तेरा\".

text: आज बहुत थक गया हूँ, बस सीधा सोना चाहता हूँ।
expected_pronunciation_notes: Casual declarative; common contraction \"सीधा\".

text: तुझे पता है कल मीटिंग कितने बजे है?
expected_pronunciation_notes: Informal question; \"मीटिंग\" is an English loanword in Devanagari.

text: अरे यार, मेरा फ़ोन कहाँ रखा था?!
expected_pronunciation_notes: Exclamative question; everyday casual reaction.

text: kal mujhe office jaana hai
expected_pronunciation_notes: Should sound Hindi, NOT English. \"office\" is the only English word.

text: mera naam Arjun hai aur mai Bengaluru se hu
expected_pronunciation_notes: \"hai\" is Hindi \"is\", NOT \"hi\" greeting. \"Bengaluru\" must be pronounced Indian, not anglicized.

text: yaar tu kal kya kar raha tha
expected_pronunciation_notes: Casual Hinglish, common words yaar/tu/kya.

text: kya tu bhi aaj party me aa raha hai?
expected_pronunciation_notes: Roman-script Hindi question with English loan \"party\".

text: abe yaar jaldi reply kar, mai wait kar raha hu
expected_pronunciation_notes: Roman-Hindi imperative; \"reply\" and \"wait\" must NOT be re-anglicized in pronunciation.

text: kal raat ka movie tha bohot bakwaas, paisa bilkul waste
expected_pronunciation_notes: Casual film reaction; multiple English loans inside Roman-Hindi.

text: tera laptop kab tak deliver hoga bhai?
expected_pronunciation_notes: Roman-Hindi question with English nouns \"laptop\" / \"deliver\".

text: yaar tu bohot lucky hai, mujhe nahi mila ticket!
expected_pronunciation_notes: Casual exclamation; \"hai\" must read as Hindi \"is\", not \"hi\".

text: Kal mujhe ऑफिस जाना hai, but ट्राफिक will be an issue.
expected_pronunciation_notes: The hardest case — script switches mid-sentence.

text: Mera presentation tomorrow है, और मैं nervous हूं।
expected_pronunciation_notes: Hindi grammar around English content words.

text: Bhai please मेरा homework कर दे, मैं तुझे ₹100 दूंगा।
expected_pronunciation_notes: Currency symbol + Devanagari numerals/script switch.

text: Tumne वो new restaurant try kiya jo Connaught Place में khula hai?
expected_pronunciation_notes: Mid-sentence script switch with question intonation.

text: कल का event cancel हो गया, सबको message कर देना please।
expected_pronunciation_notes: English content nouns inside Hindi grammatical frame.

text: Boss को बता देना kal मैं leave पर रहूँगा, kuch personal काम है।
expected_pronunciation_notes: Heavy code-switching; office register; double script switches.

text: Ye file को quickly review करो, deadline बहुत close है।
expected_pronunciation_notes: Imperative with English verb embedded in Hindi auxiliary structure.

text: My friend Aishwarya from Chennai is visiting Bengaluru next week.
expected_pronunciation_notes: Three Indian named entities in pure-English sentence.

text: Mr. Khanna will join the meeting after he finishes lunch with Priya.
expected_pronunciation_notes: Indian surname + first name in English context.

text: I love butter chicken from Karim's in Old Delhi.
expected_pronunciation_notes: Restaurant + locality, Indian food name.

text: Office में सब log lunch के लिए बाहर गए, तू भी आ ja yaar.
expected_pronunciation_notes: Office casual register; English content nouns inside Hindi frame.

text: Rohan is flying from Mumbai to Bengaluru tomorrow morning for work.
expected_pronunciation_notes: Three Indian named entities (one personal, two cities) in English.

text: Let's grab biryani from Paradise in Hyderabad this weekend.
expected_pronunciation_notes: Indian food + restaurant + city in English context.

text: She just got hired at Tata Consultancy Services in Pune.
expected_pronunciation_notes: Indian company brand in pure-English sentence.
